messages:
Mira: Kicking off a short design thread for the benchmark visuals + copy. Goal: webinar slide deck that convinces product teams to think in 'cost per active session' and shows where latency becomes a business leak. Need 3 main visuals, 2 one-liners, and a tiny routing-to-archetype cheat sheet. Who can take which?
James: I'm in. Visuals I'd propose: A) Latency vs $/1M with a highlighted UX-knee band B) Cost-per-session vs cache hit % (simulated curve) C) SLA buckets showing p95 latency vs throughput (stacked bars).
Alex: I'll own the econ cheat sheet (tiny table mapping routing policy -> expected $/session and p95). Keep numbers rounded, add a footnote with assumptions. Also recommend a single CTA per slide.
Sophia: I'll write the two-sentence hooks and micro-copy. Draft hooks: 1) "Stop guessing your inference bill  measure cost where users actually feel it." 2) "Pick SLAs that match your product: don't overpay for eye-blink speed if users don't need it."
beth_marketing: For inbound, let's add ?seg=latency and ?seg=econ UTMs and a hidden form field for SLA preference. Also want 1 social card line: "How teams halve inference spend without breaking UX."
benchbot: Uploaded baseline csv: https://redwood.share/bench/2240012345-baseline.csv (models A/B/C, p50/p95, token cost, cache-sim). Also added a cache-sweep sim file.
Mira: Nice. @ana can you run a batching vs no-batching slice at 500 qps + 2k qps and drop p95 + $/1M tokens? We need numbers for slide A and the econ cheat sheet.
nana: on it. ETA 5pm PT. I'll put results under the same folder and post summary.
James: Chart style notes: use single continuous lines, max 3 colors, label knee with a callout, add shaded band "Good UX" between 0-150ms for consumer chat and 0-75ms for realtime typing demo. Avoid gridlines except subtle x-axis ticks.
Sophia: For captions: A) "Latency bites budgets: the knee is where UX expectations and dollar signs meet." B) "Caching amplifies value: small hit-rate lifts reduce $/session markedly." C) "SLAs are tradeoffs: faster p95s usually mean lower headroom for throughput."
Alex: Routing cheat sheet draft (short): [Routing policy] -> [When to use] -> [Est. $/session]. I'll keep as 3 rows: Low-latency, Balanced, Cost-optimized.
diego: Quick UX note: for chart A, instead of log y I'd prefer linear with a cropped top and a note for outliers. Users read linear scales easier.
Mira: Good point @diego — can we show a log inset if needed? small box with log scale for long tail.
James: Yea add an inset for the high-cost tail. Also annotate the models we tested (A/B/C) next to lines.
benchbot: Added a precomputed knee detection column in the csv and a small png suggestion for annotation: https://redwood.share/bench/2240012345-annot.png
Sophia: Social blurbs (short options): "Stop letting latency surprise your infra bill. Join our webinar." OR "Measure inference in $/session, not tokens. Free webinar." Use #redwoodwebinar.
beth_marketing: I'll prep a 2-line email subject + preview text once captions are locked. Suggest: Subject: "How to cut inference costs without degrading UX" Preview: "Real numbers, routing playbooks, and a free cheat sheet."
Mira: Timeline: visuals + captions + cheat sheet by tomorrow 11:00am PT. I'll assemble slides and a one-pager for sales. Can everyone confirm?
Alex: Confirmed, will drop table by 9pm tonight so you can review.
nana: Batching sims done at 4:50pm PT, uploading now.
benchbot: Uploaded batching results: https://redwood.share/bench/2240012345-batching.csv
Mira: Thanks all. If anyone has a short customer quote about trading latency for cost, DM me. Otherwise I'll draft a hypothetical micro-case for the one-pager and mark it as "example".
Sophia: I'll add final captions + alt social lines by 9am PT. :sparkles:
beth_marketing: Once captions are final I'll map CTA variants to audience segments and share the UTM table.
Mira: Great work  Ill share a slide skeleton by 8am with placeholders. Closing thread for updates inside the deck comments.
